+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

 500: \begin{remark}[What the decomposition resolves]
 501: When \(d+\alpha\le4\), one has \(p_{\alpha,d}=2\), so every
 502: finite-covariance law makes the tail energy \(o(s^{-4})\) by
 503: Theorem~\ref{thm:high-dimensional-kl-moment-threshold}.  When
 504: \(d+\alpha>4\), finite covariance alone need not do so.  In that regime
 505: \eqref{eq:stable-law-by-law-criterion} is the exact missing law-by-law
 506: condition: it neither replaces the nonlinear tail energy by a moment nor
 507: assumes regular variation.
 508: \end{remark}
 509: 
 510: The finite-covariance proof above uses positivity of the one-sided raw-tail
 511: potential.  At higher order the natural object is a pair of laws, and the
 512: difference of their raw-tail potentials is signed.  Applying \(\Phi\) to that
 513: difference would therefore neither be well-defined in general nor preserve
 514: nonnegativity.  The following relative \(\Phi\)-energy is the replacement.
 515: 
 516: \input{sec_two_background_kl_lemma}
 517: 
 518: \begin{theorem}[Arbitrary-order law-by-law tail-defect decomposition]
 519: \label{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}
 520: Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), and let \(r\ge1\) be an integer.  Let
 521: \(\nu,\eta\) be probability laws on \(\RR^d\) satisfying
 522: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-moment-hypotheses}
 523:  m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
 524:  \qquad
 525:  \int_{\RR^d}|x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
 526: \end{equation}
 527: For \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), put
 528: \[
 529:  \tau_s^\lambda=\lambda(|x|>s),\qquad
 530:  V_s^\lambda(y)=\int_{\{|x|>s\}}
 531:  F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
 532: \]
 533: and use the moment modes \(B_j^\lambda\) from
 534: \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}.  Their values agree for \(j<r\);
 535: write
 536: \[
 537:  C_{r-1,s}(y)=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_j^\nu(y)
 538:              =\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_j^\eta(y),
 539: \]
 540: with an empty sum when \(r=1\), and define
 541: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-quotients}
 542:  A_s^\lambda(y)=1+C_{r-1,s}(y)+V_s^\lambda(y)-\tau_s^\lambda.
 543: \end{equation}
 544: For all sufficiently large \(s\), both \(A_s^\lambda\) are positive,
 545: integrate to one against \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), and hence define probability
 546: densities
 547: \[
 548:  k_{r,s}^\lambda(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)
 549:                     A_s^\lambda(x/s).
 550: \]
 551: The nonnegative raw-tail defect energy
 552: \begin{align}
 553:  \mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
 554:  &:=D_{\rm KL}(k_{r,s}^\nu\|k_{r,s}^\eta)\notag\\
 555:  &=\int_{\RR^d}A_s^\eta
 556:  \Phi\!\left(\frac{A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta}{A_s^\eta}\right)
 557:  \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 558:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy}
 559: \end{align}
 560: is finite, and, with
 561: \(\Delta_r=\int x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)\), one has
 562: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}
 563:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 564:  =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
 565:   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
 566: \end{equation}
 567: In particular, law by law,
 568: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion}
 569:  s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 570:  \longrightarrow\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
 571:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 572:  s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
 573: \end{equation}
 574: No regular-variation or absolute-continuity hypothesis, and no moment above
 575: order \(r\), is required.
 576: \end{theorem}
 577: 
 578: \begin{proof}
 579: Write \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\), \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), and let
 580: \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be the homogeneous degree-\(j\) Taylor term of
 581: \(F_y(z)\) at zero.  The stable-kernel estimates in
 582: Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}, Taylor's formula, and
 583: translation continuity of \(D^rp_1\) in \(L^1\) give, for \(|z|\le1\),
 584: \begin{align}
 585:  &\left\|F_\cdot(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r\mathsf B_j(\cdot,z)\right\|_\infty
 586:  +\left\|F_\cdot(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r\mathsf B_j(\cdot,z)
 587:   \right\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 588:  \le\varepsilon_r(|z|)|z|^r,
 589:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder}\\
 590:  &\|\mathsf B_j(\cdot,z)\|_\infty
 591:  +\|\mathsf B_j(\cdot,z)\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 592:  \le C_r|z|^j,\qquad 1\le j\le r,
 593:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}
 594: \end{align}
 595: where \(\varepsilon_r\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
 596: zero.  For the uniform part one may use the bounded order-\((r+1)\)
 597: derivative quotient, giving the stronger \(O(|z|^{r+1})\) bound.  For the
 598: \(L^1\) part, multiplication by \(p_1(y)\) reduces the integral remainder
 599: to translates of \(D^rp_1\), exactly as in
 600: \eqref{eq:stable-local-taylor-modulus}.
 601: 
 602: Set
 603: \[
 604:  q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
 605: \]
 606: Splitting the integral at \(|x|=s\), retaining the raw exterior translate,
 607: and using the moment identities gives the exact decomposition
 608: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-exact-quotient-split}
 609:  q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}B_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda.
 610: \end{equation}
 611: Here \(R_s^\lambda\) is the interior Taylor remainder through order \(r\)
 612: minus the exterior Taylor modes of orders \(1,\ldots,r\).  Equations
 613: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} and
 614: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} imply
 615: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness}
 616:  \|R_s^\lambda\|_\infty+
 617:  \|R_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
 618: \end{equation}
 619: Indeed, after multiplication by \(s^r\), the interior term is dominated by
 620: \(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero, while for \(j\le r\),
 621: \[
 622:  s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
 623:  \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}).
 624: \]
 625: The same last estimate gives
 626: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness}
 627:  \tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r}).
 628: \end{equation}
 629: 
 630: Translation preserves mass, so
 631: \[
 632:  V_s^\lambda\ge0,\qquad
 633:  \int V_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=\tau_s^\lambda.
 634: \]
 635: Also \(\int B_j^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0\), by integration of the
 636: derivatives in \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}.  Therefore
 637: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-normalization}
 638:  \int A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=1.
 639: \end{equation}
 640: Moreover,
 641: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}
 642:  \inf_yA_s^\lambda(y)
 643:  \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1,
 644: \end{equation}
 645: because \(V_s^\lambda\ge0\),
 646: \(\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty=O(s^{-1})\) (with value zero when \(r=1\)), and
 647: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness} holds.  This proves positivity,
 648: including at \(r=1\), and gives a common lower bound such as \(1/2\).
 649: 
 650: We next prove proxy-entropy finiteness without appealing to the covariance
 651: case.  The two-sided stable-density bound in
 652: Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} and
 653: \(1+|w+z|\le(1+|w|)(1+|z|)\) give
 654: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy}
 655:  D_{\rm KL}\!\left(p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)\,\middle\|\,p_1\right)
 656:  \le C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|).
 657: \end{equation}
 658: If \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), write \(V_s^\lambda=\tau_s^\lambda Q_s^\lambda\),
 659: where \(Q_s^\lambda\) is the quotient, relative to \(p_1\), of the
 660: normalized exterior translate mixture.  Convexity of relative entropy and
 661: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy} imply
 662: \begin{align}
 663:  \int Q_s^\lambda\log Q_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 664:  &\le\frac1{\tau_s^\lambda}\int_{|x|>s}
 665:  \left\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|x|/s)\right\}
 666:  \lambda(\dd x)\notag\\
 667:  &<\infty,
 668:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}
 669: \end{align}
 670: since \(\log(1+|x|/s)\le |x|/s\) and the assumed \(r\)-th moment, with
 671: \(r\ge1\), supplies a finite first moment.  For \(0\le\tau\le1\),
 672: \(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\); hence
 673: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}, together with the bound
 674: of the negative part of \(q\log q\), proves
 675: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite}
 676:  \int\Phi(V_s^\lambda)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
 677: \end{equation}
 678: The conclusion is immediate when \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\).
 679: 
 680: For large \(s\), \(|C_{r-1,s}-\tau_s^\lambda|\le1/2\), so
 681: \(A_s^\lambda\le3/2+V_s^\lambda\).  The elementary bound
 682: \[
 683:  (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
 684:  \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
 685: \]
 686: and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite} show that
 687: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite}
 688:  \int A_s^\lambda\log^+A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
 689: \end{equation}
 690: Finally \(A_s^\eta\ge1/2\).  The positive part of
 691: \(A_s^\nu\log(A_s^\nu/A_s^\eta)\) is bounded by
 692: \(A_s^\nu\log^+(2A_s^\nu)\), while its negative part is bounded in absolute
 693: integral by \(e^{-1}\int A_s^\eta\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=e^{-1}\).
 694: Thus \(\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)<\infty\), as asserted.
 695: 
 696: It remains to verify, rather than assume, the hypotheses of the abstract
 697: two-background KL perturbation lemma.  Put
 698: \(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\), take
 699: \[
 700:  (A_{1,s},A_{2,s})=(A_s^\nu,A_s^\eta),\qquad
 701:  (B_{1,s},B_{2,s})=(B_r^\nu,B_r^\eta),
 702:  \qquad (R_{1,s},R_{2,s})=(R_s^\nu,R_s^\eta).
 703: \]
 704: The modes \(B_r^\lambda\) are bounded by
 705: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}, and their integrals vanish.  The first
 706: requested background estimate follows directly from the common jet and the
 707: exact tail normalization:
 708: \begin{align}
 709:  \|A_s^\lambda-1\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 710:  &\le\|C_{r-1,s}\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}

 714:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-background-to-one}
 715: \end{align}
 716: For \(r=1\), the sum is empty and the same proof applies.  For the second

 718: \begin{align}
 719:  \|A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}

 722:  &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
 723:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-two-background-separation}
 724: \end{align}
 725: This is the place where retaining the common lower-order jet removes every
 726: interior contribution from the difference of the backgrounds.

 734:  \ge e^{-L\EE_\lambda|X|/s}\longrightarrow1

 736: uniformly in \(y\).  Thus the actual quotients have a common positive lower
 737: bound.  Their exact split is
 738: \(q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+\epsilon_sB_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda\),
 739: and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness} supplies the required
 740: \(L^1\) and \(L^\infty\) smallness.  Finally,
 741: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite} verifies the finite
 742: positive entropy hypothesis.  All hypotheses of the two-background KL
 743: perturbation lemma are now proved.  Its conclusion gives
 744: \[
 745:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 746:  =\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
 747:  +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta)^2
 748:        \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}+o(s^{-2r}).
 749: \]
 750: By \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode},
 751: \(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the quadratic integral is
 752: \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves
 753: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}.  Formula
 754: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy} is a relative \(\Phi\)-entropy and
 755: is therefore nonnegative; the equivalence
 756: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion} follows immediately.
 757: 
 758: The raw-tail split, its normalization, and the finite-moment dominated
 759: convergence are exactly the steps that survive from the covariance proof.
 760: The new step is the two-background expansion above: it retains the common
 761: lower-order jet inside both positive tail proxies and replaces the
 762: unavailable one-sided \(\Phi\)-energy of a signed tail difference by a
 763: relative \(\Phi\)-energy.  When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is
 764: centred, this energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\),
 765: which differs from the energy in
 766: Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
 767:  in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 768: \end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}
