+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
+entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
+tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact

+defensible first target.

+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work.  All-order

+authors' knowledge, the new result is the stable law-by-law nonnegative
+proxy-KL decomposition under only finite \(r\)-th moments, with its exact
+vanishing criterion.  The manuscript makes no uniqueness or canonicity claim
+for the proxy.

-Niles-Weed already proved the arbitrary first-unmatched-moment KL mechanism
-for Gaussian smoothing under sub-Gaussian tails. The paper excludes the

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

 ## Fit Rationale
 
-The paper's central result is an exact large-scale relative-entropy
-asymptotic for convolution with isotropic strictly stable kernels. Its main
-analytic inputs are two-sided fractional heat-kernel bounds, derivative
-quotients, critical weighted translate estimates, and a nonlinear Bregman
-transfer. The endpoint moment theorem and its moving-ball counterexamples
-are therefore aimed directly at readers working on stable semigroups,
-nonlocal potential theory, fractional diffusion, and probabilistic analytic
-inequalities. These subjects are a closer match to *Potential Analysis* than
-to a broad functional-analysis venue.
+The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
+entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
+tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact
+coefficient-attainment criterion.  The proof rests on critical weighted
+translate estimates, \(L^1/L^\infty/L^q\) transfer, Bregman geometry, and a
+two-background Hessian argument.  This analytic architecture and its
+nonlocal-semigroup applications make the Journal of Functional Analysis a
+defensible first target.
+
+The priority boundary is narrow.  Chen and Niles-Weed's arbitrary-order
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work.  All-order
+stable/fractional heat-kernel density expansions are also prior work,
+including those of Ishige, Kawakami, and Michihisa.  To the best of the
+authors' knowledge, the new result is the stable law-by-law nonnegative
+proxy-KL decomposition under only finite \(r\)-th moments, with its exact
+vanishing criterion.  The manuscript makes no uniqueness or canonicity claim
+for the proxy.
 
-The result is positioned as a strong specialist contribution. Chen and
-Niles-Weed already proved the arbitrary first-unmatched-moment KL mechanism
-for Gaussian smoothing under sub-Gaussian tails. The paper excludes the
-Gaussian endpoint and contributes the heavy-tailed range
-\(0<\alpha<2\): the optimal complete-moment exponent, endpoint sufficiency,
-and analytic uniform sharpness over the full moment class. In the
-non-Hilbert regime the sharpness construction retains a finite nonzero
-leading tensor; in the Hilbert regime the lower threshold is only
-coefficient-domain minimality.
+Acceptance at JFA remains uncertain on presentation, breadth, and priority.
+The uncertainty is not that the central increment is below the journal's
+theorem-level standard.  The Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare,
+Probabilites et Statistiques remains a natural alternative because the
+results also address stable laws, moment thresholds, and entropy asymptotics

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible â†’ gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI â†’ build â†’ signing, API â†’ service â†’ database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets â†’ workflow âœ“, workflow â†’ build âœ—)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes â†’ Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If â‰¥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultrathink this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms â‰  understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
+entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
+tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact
+coefficient-attainment criterion.  The proof rests on critical weighted
+translate estimates, \(L^1/L^\infty/L^q\) transfer, Bregman geometry, and a
+two-background Hessian argument.  This analytic architecture and its
+nonlocal-semigroup applications make the Journal of Functional Analysis a
+defensible first target.

+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work.  All-order

+authors' knowledge, the new result is the stable law-by-law nonnegative
+proxy-KL decomposition under only finite \(r\)-th moments, with its exact
+vanishing criterion.  The manuscript makes no uniqueness or canonicity claim
+for the proxy.

-Niles-Weed already proved the arbitrary first-unmatched-moment KL mechanism
-for Gaussian smoothing under sub-Gaussian tails. The paper excludes the

+Acceptance at JFA remains uncertain on presentation, breadth, and priority.
+The uncertainty is not that the central increment is below the journal's

+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+The novelty claim is correspondingly narrow.  Arbitrary-order Gaussian
+first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work, and all-order
+stable/fractional density expansions are prior work.  To the best of our

+of two explicit positive tail-jet proxies, under only finite \(r\)-th

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

 ## Fit Rationale
 
-The paper's central result is an exact large-scale relative-entropy
-asymptotic for convolution with isotropic strictly stable kernels. Its main
-analytic inputs are two-sided fractional heat-kernel bounds, derivative
-quotients, critical weighted translate estimates, and a nonlinear Bregman
-transfer. The endpoint moment theorem and its moving-ball counterexamples
-are therefore aimed directly at readers working on stable semigroups,
-nonlocal potential theory, fractional diffusion, and probabilistic analytic
-inequalities. These subjects are a closer match to *Potential Analysis* than
-to a broad functional-analysis venue.
+The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
+entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
+tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact
+coefficient-attainment criterion.  The proof rests on critical weighted
+translate estimates, \(L^1/L^\infty/L^q\) transfer, Bregman geometry, and a
+two-background Hessian argument.  This analytic architecture and its
+nonlocal-semigroup applications make the Journal of Functional Analysis a
+defensible first target.
+
+The priority boundary is narrow.  Chen and Niles-Weed's arbitrary-order
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work.  All-order
+stable/fractional heat-kernel density expansions are also prior work,
+including those of Ishige, Kawakami, and Michihisa.  To the best of the
+authors' knowledge, the new result is the stable law-by-law nonnegative
+proxy-KL decomposition under only finite \(r\)-th moments, with its exact
+vanishing criterion.  The manuscript makes no uniqueness or canonicity claim
+for the proxy.
 
-The result is positioned as a strong specialist contribution. Chen and
-Niles-Weed already proved the arbitrary first-unmatched-moment KL mechanism
-for Gaussian smoothing under sub-Gaussian tails. The paper excludes the
-Gaussian endpoint and contributes the heavy-tailed range
-\(0<\alpha<2\): the optimal complete-moment exponent, endpoint sufficiency,
-and analytic uniform sharpness over the full moment class. In the
-non-Hilbert regime the sharpness construction retains a finite nonzero
-leading tensor; in the Hilbert regime the lower threshold is only
-coefficient-domain minimality.
+Acceptance at JFA remains uncertain on presentation, breadth, and priority.
+The uncertainty is not that the central increment is below the journal's
+theorem-level standard.  The Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare,
+Probabilites et Statistiques remains a natural alternative because the
+results also address stable laws, moment thresholds, and entropy asymptotics
+as probability questions.

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, take the finite-support probability blocks
+\(A_R^+,A_R^-\) of
+Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks} and convolve both with the
+same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula shows that the
+convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their order-
+\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every other
+term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

 ## Fit Rationale
 
-The paper's central result is an exact large-scale relative-entropy
-asymptotic for convolution with isotropic strictly stable kernels. Its main
-analytic inputs are two-sided fractional heat-kernel bounds, derivative
-quotients, critical weighted translate estimates, and a nonlinear Bregman
-transfer. The endpoint moment theorem and its moving-ball counterexamples
-are therefore aimed directly at readers working on stable semigroups,
-nonlocal potential theory, fractional diffusion, and probabilistic analytic
-inequalities. These subjects are a closer match to *Potential Analysis* than
-to a broad functional-analysis venue.
+The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
+entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
+tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact
+coefficient-attainment criterion.  The proof rests on critical weighted
+translate estimates, \(L^1/L^\infty/L^q\) transfer, Bregman geometry, and a
+two-background Hessian argument.  This analytic architecture and its
+nonlocal-semigroup applications make the Journal of Functional Analysis a
+defensible first target.
+
+The priority boundary is narrow.  Chen and Niles-Weed's arbitrary-order
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work.  All-order
+stable/fractional heat-kernel density expansions are also prior work,
+including those of Ishige, Kawakami, and Michihisa.  To the best of the
+authors' knowledge, the new result is the stable law-by-law nonnegative
+proxy-KL decomposition under only finite \(r\)-th moments, with its exact
+vanishing criterion.  The manuscript makes no uniqueness or canonicity claim
+for the proxy.
 
-The result is positioned as a strong specialist contribution. Chen and
-Niles-Weed already proved the arbitrary first-unmatched-moment KL mechanism
-for Gaussian smoothing under sub-Gaussian tails. The paper excludes the
-Gaussian endpoint and contributes the heavy-tailed range
-\(0<\alpha<2\): the optimal complete-moment exponent, endpoint sufficiency,
-and analytic uniform sharpness over the full moment class. In the
-non-Hilbert regime the sharpness construction retains a finite nonzero
-leading tensor; in the Hilbert regime the lower threshold is only
-coefficient-domain minimality.
+Acceptance at JFA remains uncertain on presentation, breadth, and priority.
+The uncertainty is not that the central increment is below the journal's
+theorem-level standard.  The Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare,
+Probabilites et Statistiques remains a natural alternative because the
+results also address stable laws, moment thresholds, and entropy asymptotics
+as probability questions.
