+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, use the finite-support probability blocks
+from Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}.  Convolve \(A_R^+\) and
+\(A_R^-\) with the same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula
+shows that the convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their
+order-\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every
+other term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

 ## Fit Rationale
 
-The paper's central result is an exact large-scale relative-entropy
-asymptotic for convolution with isotropic strictly stable kernels. Its main
-analytic inputs are two-sided fractional heat-kernel bounds, derivative
-quotients, critical weighted translate estimates, and a nonlinear Bregman
-transfer. The endpoint moment theorem and its moving-ball counterexamples
-are therefore aimed directly at readers working on stable semigroups,
-nonlocal potential theory, fractional diffusion, and probabilistic analytic
-inequalities. These subjects are a closer match to *Potential Analysis* than
-to a broad functional-analysis venue.
+The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
+entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
+tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact
+coefficient-attainment criterion.  The proof rests on critical weighted
+translate estimates, \(L^1/L^\infty/L^q\) transfer, Bregman geometry, and a
+two-background Hessian argument.  This analytic architecture and its
+nonlocal-semigroup applications make the Journal of Functional Analysis a
+defensible first target.
+
+The priority boundary is narrow.  Chen and Niles-Weed's arbitrary-order
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work.  All-order
+stable/fractional heat-kernel density expansions are also prior work,
+including those of Ishige, Kawakami, and Michihisa.  To the best of the
+authors' knowledge, the new result is the stable law-by-law nonnegative
+proxy-KL decomposition under only finite \(r\)-th moments, with its exact
+vanishing criterion.  The manuscript makes no uniqueness or canonicity claim
+for the proxy.
 
-The result is positioned as a strong specialist contribution. Chen and
-Niles-Weed already proved the arbitrary first-unmatched-moment KL mechanism
-for Gaussian smoothing under sub-Gaussian tails. The paper excludes the
-Gaussian endpoint and contributes the heavy-tailed range
-\(0<\alpha<2\): the optimal complete-moment exponent, endpoint sufficiency,
-and analytic uniform sharpness over the full moment class. In the
-non-Hilbert regime the sharpness construction retains a finite nonzero
-leading tensor; in the Hilbert regime the lower threshold is only
-coefficient-domain minimality.
+Acceptance at JFA remains uncertain on presentation, breadth, and priority.
+The uncertainty is not that the central increment is below the journal's
+theorem-level standard.  The Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare,
+Probabilites et Statistiques remains a natural alternative because the
+results also address stable laws, moment thresholds, and entropy asymptotics
+as probability questions.

def counterexample_search() -> Dict[str, object]:
    rows = []
    false_classifications = []
    for a in np.linspace(-0.5, 2.0, 26):
        law = LogParetoBoundary(4, float(a))
        integral_diverges = a <= 1.0
        moment_finite = law.boundary_moment_finite()
        classification_ok = moment_finite == (not integral_diverges)
        row = {
            "a": float(a),
            "integrated_factor_diverges": integral_diverges,
            "p_moment_finite": moment_finite,
            "classification_ok": classification_ok,
        }
        rows.append(row)
        if not classification_ok:
            false_classifications.append(row)
    return {
        "candidates": len(rows),
        "false_classifications": false_classifications,
        "finite-boundary-example": {
            "a": 1.5,
            "meaning": (
                "tail index remains p, but integral L(s) ds/s converges and "
                "the p-th moment is finite"
            ),
        },
        "passed": not false_classifications,
    }


def _run_verification() -> int:
    sections = {
        "laurent_constants": verify_constants(),
        "tauberian_moments": verify_moments(),
        "quotient_jets": verify_quotient_jets(),
        "full_entropy": verify_full_entropy(),
        "counterexample_search": counterexample_search(),
    }
    failures = []
    for name, section in sections.items():
        if isinstance(section, list):
            failures.extend(
                f"{name}:{row.get('law', row.get('N'))}"
                for row in section
                if not row["passed"]
            )
        elif not section["passed"]:
            failures.append(name)

    print("REGULAR-VARIATION BOUNDARY-LAYER VERIFICATION")
    for name, section in sections.items():
        print(f"\n[{name}]")
        if isinstance(section, list):
            for row in section:
                print(row)
        else:
            print(section)
    print(f"\nfailures={failures}")
    print("RESULT: PASS" if not failures else "RESULT: FAIL")
    return 0 if not failures else 1


def main(argv=()) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.output is None:
        return _run_verification()

    capture = StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(capture):
        status = _run_verification()
    report = capture.getvalue()
    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(report, end="")
    return status

def _format_report(report: dict) -> str:
    lines = [
        report["description"],
        f"orders m={report['m_range'][0]}..{report['m_range'][1]}",
        f"quadrature={report['quadrature']}",
        "",
        "FINITE/BOUNDARY BATTERY",
    ]
    for row in report["checks"]:
        lines.append(
            f"m={row['m']} p={row['moment_order']} law={row['law']} "
            f"moment_finite={row['moment_finite']} passed={row['passed']}"
        )
        lines.append("  t=" + ", ".join(f"{x:g}" for x in row["times"]))
        lines.append(
            "  t^(2m) residual=" + ", ".join(f"{x:.10g}" for x in row["scaled_residual"])
        )
        if row["moment_finite"]:
            lines.append(f"  exact A_(2m)={row['exact_A']:.10g}")
        else:
            lines.append(
                f"  expected={row['expected_boundary_behavior']}, sign={row['expected_sign']}"
            )
    lines.extend(["", "EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE SEARCH"])
    for row in report["counterexample_search"]:
        lines.append(
            f"m={row['m']} law={row['law']} exact={row['exact_A']:.8g} "
            f"last_scaled={row['scaled_residual'][-1]:.8g} passed={row['passed']}"
        )
    lines.extend(
        [
            "",
            f"failed battery checks: {len(report['failed_checks'])}",
            f"counterexamples found: {len(report['counterexamples'])}",
            "RESULT: PASS" if not report["failed_checks"] and not report["counterexamples"] else "RESULT: FAIL",
        ]
    )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=()) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true", help="smaller deterministic test battery")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="emit JSON instead of the text report")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="write the report with LF line endings")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    report = run_battery(quick=args.quick)

    else:

        args.output.write_text(formatted, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        print(formatted, end="")

        radial_ok = radial_ok and row_ok
        radial_rows.append(f"d={d}: relative errors={errors}")
    checks.append(
        Check(
            "critical clustered-shell vague Riemann sums",
            radial_ok,
            "; ".join(radial_rows),
        )
    )

    rate_rows = []
    rate_ok = True
    log_times = (8.0, 16.0, 32.0, 64.0)
    for d in (4, 10, 11, 12, 40):
        p_d = 4.0 * (d + 1) / (d + 5)
        if d == 11:
            ratios = [math.exp(-value) * value**2 for value in log_times]
        else:
            ratios = [
                math.exp((2.0 - p_d) * value) * value
                for value in log_times
            ]
        row_ok = all(
            ratios[index + 1] < ratios[index]
            for index in range(len(ratios) - 1)
        ) and ratios[-1] < 1.0e-3
        rate_ok = rate_ok and row_ok
        rate_rows.append(f"d={d}: normalized remainder rates={ratios}")
    checks.append(
        Check(
            "critical diffuse remainder decay including d=11",
            rate_ok,
            "; ".join(rate_rows),
        )
    )

    bernoulli_rows = []
    bernoulli_ok = True
    for atom_mass in np.geomspace(1.0e-9, 1.0e-2, 16):
        convolved_mass = 0.4 * atom_mass
        reference_mass = 0.02 * atom_mass
        divergence = (
            convolved_mass * math.log(convolved_mass / reference_mass)
            + (1.0 - convolved_mass)
            * math.log(
                (1.0 - convolved_mass) / (1.0 - reference_mass)
            )
        )
        ratio = divergence / atom_mass
        bernoulli_rows.append(ratio)
        bernoulli_ok = bernoulli_ok and ratio > 0.75
    checks.append(
        Check(
            "critical cluster Bernoulli entropy lower bound",
            bernoulli_ok,
            f"D(Ber(0.4a)||Ber(0.02a))/a range="
            f"[{min(bernoulli_rows)}, {max(bernoulli_rows)}]",
        )
    )
    return checks


def run(quick: bool) -> list[Check]:
    return (
        symbolic_checks()
        + [
            critical_bregman_check(),
            two_background_bregman_transfer_check(),
            covariance_proxy_quadrature_check(quick),
        ]
        + [finite_covariance_proxy_check(quick)]
        + [
            raw_tail_poisson_energy_check(quick),
            moving_annulus_comparability_check(),
            pre_phi_thin_shell_aggregation_check(),
        ]
        + numerical_moment_matching_checks(quick)
        + [pareto_square_boundary_check(quick)]
        + critical_vague_tail_checks()
    )


def _run_verification(argv=()) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    checks = run(args.quick)
    print("ORACLE A2 INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION")
    for check in checks:
        print(f"[{check.name}] {'PASS' if check.passed else 'FAIL'}")
        print(f"  {check.evidence}")
    failures = [check.name for check in checks if not check.passed]
    print(f"failures={failures}")
    print("RESULT: PASS" if not failures else "RESULT: FAIL")
    return 0 if not failures else 1


def main(argv=()) -> int:
    output_parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    output_parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    archive_args, remaining = output_parser.parse_known_args(argv)
    if archive_args.output is None:
        return _run_verification(remaining)

    capture = StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(capture):
        status = _run_verification(remaining)
    report = capture.getvalue()
    archive_args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    archive_args.output.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(report, end="")
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, use the finite-support probability blocks
+from Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}.  Convolve \(A_R^+\) and
+\(A_R^-\) with the same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula
+shows that the convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their
+order-\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every
+other term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

 ## Fit Rationale
 
-The paper's central result is an exact large-scale relative-entropy
-asymptotic for convolution with isotropic strictly stable kernels. Its main
-analytic inputs are two-sided fractional heat-kernel bounds, derivative
-quotients, critical weighted translate estimates, and a nonlinear Bregman
-transfer. The endpoint moment theorem and its moving-ball counterexamples
-are therefore aimed directly at readers working on stable semigroups,
-nonlocal potential theory, fractional diffusion, and probabilistic analytic
-inequalities. These subjects are a closer match to *Potential Analysis* than
-to a broad functional-analysis venue.

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, use the finite-support probability blocks
+from Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}.  Convolve \(A_R^+\) and
+\(A_R^-\) with the same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula
+shows that the convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their
+order-\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every
+other term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[

+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

 ## Fit Rationale

-analytic inputs are two-sided fractional heat-kernel bounds, derivative

-nonlocal potential theory, fractional diffusion, and probabilistic analytic
-inequalities. These subjects are a closer match to *Potential Analysis* than
-to a broad functional-analysis venue.
+The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
+entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
+tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact
+coefficient-attainment criterion.  The proof rests on critical weighted
+translate estimates, \(L^1/L^\infty/L^q\) transfer, Bregman geometry, and a
+two-background Hessian argument.  This analytic architecture and its
+nonlocal-semigroup applications make the Journal of Functional Analysis a
+defensible first target.
+
+The priority boundary is narrow.  Chen and Niles-Weed's arbitrary-order
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work.  All-order
+stable/fractional heat-kernel density expansions are also prior work,
+including those of Ishige, Kawakami, and Michihisa.  To the best of the
+authors' knowledge, the new result is the stable law-by-law nonnegative
+proxy-KL decomposition under only finite \(r\)-th moments, with its exact
+vanishing criterion.  The manuscript makes no uniqueness or canonicity claim
+for the proxy.
 
-The result is positioned as a strong specialist contribution. Chen and
-Niles-Weed already proved the arbitrary first-unmatched-moment KL mechanism
-for Gaussian smoothing under sub-Gaussian tails. The paper excludes the
-Gaussian endpoint and contributes the heavy-tailed range
-\(0<\alpha<2\): the optimal complete-moment exponent, endpoint sufficiency,
-and analytic uniform sharpness over the full moment class. In the
-non-Hilbert regime the sharpness construction retains a finite nonzero
-leading tensor; in the Hilbert regime the lower threshold is only
-coefficient-domain minimality.
+Acceptance at JFA remains uncertain on presentation, breadth, and priority.
+The uncertainty is not that the central increment is below the journal's
+theorem-level standard.  The Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare,
+Probabilites et Statistiques remains a natural alternative because the
+results also address stable laws, moment thresholds, and entropy asymptotics
+as probability questions.

def counterexample_search() -> Dict[str, object]:
    rows = []
    false_classifications = []
    for a in np.linspace(-0.5, 2.0, 26):
        law = LogParetoBoundary(4, float(a))
        integral_diverges = a <= 1.0
        moment_finite = law.boundary_moment_finite()
        classification_ok = moment_finite == (not integral_diverges)
        row = {
            "a": float(a),
            "integrated_factor_diverges": integral_diverges,
            "p_moment_finite": moment_finite,
            "classification_ok": classification_ok,
        }
        rows.append(row)
        if not classification_ok:
            false_classifications.append(row)
    return {
        "candidates": len(rows),
        "false_classifications": false_classifications,
        "finite-boundary-example": {
            "a": 1.5,
            "meaning": (
                "tail index remains p, but integral L(s) ds/s converges and "
                "the p-th moment is finite"
            ),
        },
        "passed": not false_classifications,
    }


def _run_verification() -> int:
    sections = {
        "laurent_constants": verify_constants(),
        "tauberian_moments": verify_moments(),
        "quotient_jets": verify_quotient_jets(),
        "full_entropy": verify_full_entropy(),
        "counterexample_search": counterexample_search(),
    }
    failures = []
    for name, section in sections.items():
        if isinstance(section, list):
            failures.extend(
                f"{name}:{row.get('law', row.get('N'))}"
                for row in section
                if not row["passed"]
            )
        elif not section["passed"]:
            failures.append(name)

    print("REGULAR-VARIATION BOUNDARY-LAYER VERIFICATION")
    for name, section in sections.items():
        print(f"\n[{name}]")
        if isinstance(section, list):
            for row in section:
                print(row)
        else:
            print(section)
    print(f"\nfailures={failures}")
    print("RESULT: PASS" if not failures else "RESULT: FAIL")
    return 0 if not failures else 1


def main(argv=()) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.output is None:
        return _run_verification()

    capture = StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(capture):
        status = _run_verification()
    report = capture.getvalue()
    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(report, end="")
    return status

def _format_report(report: dict) -> str:
    lines = [
        report["description"],
        f"orders m={report['m_range'][0]}..{report['m_range'][1]}",
        f"quadrature={report['quadrature']}",
        "",
        "FINITE/BOUNDARY BATTERY",
    ]
    for row in report["checks"]:
        lines.append(
            f"m={row['m']} p={row['moment_order']} law={row['law']} "
            f"moment_finite={row['moment_finite']} passed={row['passed']}"
        )
        lines.append("  t=" + ", ".join(f"{x:g}" for x in row["times"]))
        lines.append(
            "  t^(2m) residual=" + ", ".join(f"{x:.10g}" for x in row["scaled_residual"])
        )
        if row["moment_finite"]:
            lines.append(f"  exact A_(2m)={row['exact_A']:.10g}")
        else:
            lines.append(
                f"  expected={row['expected_boundary_behavior']}, sign={row['expected_sign']}"
            )
    lines.extend(["", "EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE SEARCH"])
    for row in report["counterexample_search"]:
        lines.append(
            f"m={row['m']} law={row['law']} exact={row['exact_A']:.8g} "
            f"last_scaled={row['scaled_residual'][-1]:.8g} passed={row['passed']}"
        )
    lines.extend(
        [
            "",
            f"failed battery checks: {len(report['failed_checks'])}",
            f"counterexamples found: {len(report['counterexamples'])}",
            "RESULT: PASS" if not report["failed_checks"] and not report["counterexamples"] else "RESULT: FAIL",
        ]
    )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=()) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true", help="smaller deterministic test battery")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="emit JSON instead of the text report")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="write the report with LF line endings")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    report = run_battery(quick=args.quick)
    formatted = json.dumps(report, indent=2) if args.json else _format_report(report)
    if args.output is None:
        print(formatted, end="")
    else:
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(formatted, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        print(formatted, end="")
    return 0 if not report["failed_checks"] and not report["counterexamples"] else 1

def run(quick: bool) -> list[Check]:
    return (
        symbolic_checks()
        + [
            critical_bregman_check(),
            two_background_bregman_transfer_check(),
            covariance_proxy_quadrature_check(quick),
        ]
        + [finite_covariance_proxy_check(quick)]
        + [
            raw_tail_poisson_energy_check(quick),
            moving_annulus_comparability_check(),
            pre_phi_thin_shell_aggregation_check(),
        ]
        + numerical_moment_matching_checks(quick)
        + [pareto_square_boundary_check(quick)]
        + critical_vague_tail_checks()
    )


def _run_verification(argv=()) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    checks = run(args.quick)
    print("ORACLE A2 INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION")
    for check in checks:
        print(f"[{check.name}] {'PASS' if check.passed else 'FAIL'}")
        print(f"  {check.evidence}")
    failures = [check.name for check in checks if not check.passed]
    print(f"failures={failures}")
    print("RESULT: PASS" if not failures else "RESULT: FAIL")
    return 0 if not failures else 1


def main(argv=()) -> int:
    output_parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    output_parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    archive_args, remaining = output_parser.parse_known_args(argv)
    if archive_args.output is None:
        return _run_verification(remaining)

    capture = StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(capture):
        status = _run_verification(remaining)
    report = capture.getvalue()
    archive_args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    archive_args.output.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(report, end="")
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, use the finite-support probability blocks
+from Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}.  Convolve \(A_R^+\) and
+\(A_R^-\) with the same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula
+shows that the convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their
+order-\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every
+other term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, use the finite-support probability blocks
+from Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}.  Convolve \(A_R^+\) and
+\(A_R^-\) with the same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula
+shows that the convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their
+order-\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every
+other term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
+addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
+ \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
+\begin{align*}
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\end{align*}
+Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
+
+For a concrete noncompact class, use the finite-support probability blocks
+from Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}.  Convolve \(A_R^+\) and
+\(A_R^-\) with the same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula
+shows that the convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their
+order-\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every
+other term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
+convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
+\label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
+If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
+\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
+finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
+order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
+which
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
+ \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
+not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
+\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
+law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
+  +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
+\]
+The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
+side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
+forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
+\end{proof}

+stable smoothing into the universal tensor coefficient and the KL divergence
+of two explicit positive tail-jet proxies, under only finite \(r\)-th
+moments, with proxy vanishing as an exact coefficient-attainment criterion.
+We claim neither that this proxy is unique nor that it is canonical among
+possible positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Two-background KL perturbation]
+Let \((E,\Omega)\) be a probability space and let
+\(\epsilon_s\downarrow0\).  For \(i=1,2\), let \(A_{i,s}\) be probability
+densities such that, for one constant \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large
+\(s\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses}
+ A_{i,s}\ge c,\qquad
+ \|A_{i,s}-1\|_1=o(1),\qquad
+ \|A_{1,s}-A_{2,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Let \(U_{i,s}=\epsilon_sB_{i,s}\), where
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-modes}
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|B_{1,s}\|_\infty+\|B_{2,s}\|_\infty\bigr)<\infty,
+ \qquad \int B_{i,s}\dd\Omega=0.
+\end{equation}
+Suppose
+\[
+ q_{i,s}=A_{i,s}+U_{i,s}+R_{i,s}
+\]
+are probability densities, uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-remainders}
+ \|R_{i,s}\|_\infty+\|R_{i,s}\|_1=o(\epsilon_s).
+\end{equation}
+Assume also that
+\(\int A_{1,s}\log^+A_{1,s}\dd\Omega<\infty\) for every sufficiently
+large \(s\).  Then all relative entropies below are finite and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}
+ D_{\rm KL}(q_{1,s}\Omega\|q_{2,s}\Omega)
+ =D_{\rm KL}(A_{1,s}\Omega\|A_{2,s}\Omega)
+ +\frac{\epsilon_s^2}{2}
+   \int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppress \(s\), write \(P_i=A_i+U_i\), and put
+\[
+ f(a,b)=a\log(a/b)-a+b.
+\]
+For large \(s\), \(P_i\ge c/2\).  Since both \(P_i\) and \(q_i\) are
+bounded below, the segments \(P_i+tR_i\), \(0\le t\le1\), have a common
+positive lower bound.  On any such region,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-partials}
+ f_a(a,b)=\log(a/b),\qquad f_b(a,b)=1-a/b,
+ \qquad |f_a(a,b)|+|f_b(a,b)|\le C|a-b|.
+\end{equation}
+The mean-value theorem and
+\[
+ |(P_1+tR_1)-(P_2+tR_2)|
+ \le |A_1-A_2|+|U_1-U_2|+|R_1|+|R_2|
+\]
+therefore give the explicit remainder-removal bound
+\begin{align}
+ &\left|\int f(q_1,q_2)\dd\Omega-
+              \int f(P_1,P_2)\dd\Omega\right|\notag\\
+ &\quad\le
+ C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)\notag\\
+ &\qquad+C(\|R_1\|_\infty+\|R_2\|_\infty)
+          (\|R_1\|_1+\|R_2\|_1)
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders}
+\end{align}
+
+It remains to expand the two positive backgrounds.  Set
+\[
+ a_t=A_1+tU_1,\qquad b_t=A_2+tU_2,
+ \qquad H(t)=\int f(a_t,b_t)\dd\Omega.
+\]
+The zero-mean condition in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-modes} makes
+\(a_t\) and \(b_t\) probability densities.  The four quantities used in
+Taylor's formula are, explicitly,
+\begin{align}
+ H(0)&=D_{\rm KL}(A_1\Omega\|A_2\Omega),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-zero}\\
+ H'(t)&=\int\left\{U_1\log\frac{a_t}{b_t}
+            +U_2\left(1-\frac{a_t}{b_t}\right)\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}\\
+ H''(t)&=\int\left\{\frac{U_1^2}{a_t}
+       -\frac{2U_1U_2}{b_t}+\frac{a_tU_2^2}{b_t^2}\right\}\dd\Omega,
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second}\\
+ H'''(t)&=\int\left\{-\frac{U_1^3}{a_t^2}
+       +\frac{3U_1U_2^2}{b_t^2}
+       -\frac{2a_tU_2^3}{b_t^3}\right\}\dd\Omega.
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third}
+\end{align}
+These formulas follow by direct differentiation; the estimates below also
+provide an integrable majorant and hence justify differentiation under the
+integral.
+
+At \(t=0\), the two coefficients in \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-first}
+are bounded by \(C|A_1-A_2|\).  Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation}
+ |H'(0)|\le
+ C(\|U_1\|_\infty+\|U_2\|_\infty)\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+For the Hessian, the lower bound in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hypotheses} gives
+\begin{align}
+ \left\|\frac1{A_i}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-1}\|A_i-1\|_1=o(1),
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-inverse-coefficient}\\
+ \left\|\frac{A_1}{A_2^2}-1\right\|_1
+ &\le c^{-2}\|A_1-A_2\|_1
+      +c^{-1}\|A_2-1\|_1=o(1).
+ \label{eq:abstract-two-background-third-coefficient}
+\end{align}
+Indeed, the second line uses
+\(A_1/A_2^2-1=(A_1-A_2)/A_2^2+(1/A_2-1)\).
+Since \(\|U_i\|_\infty=O(\epsilon_s)\), these coefficient estimates in
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-second} yield
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}
+ H''(0)=\int(U_1-U_2)^2\dd\Omega+o(\epsilon_s^2)
+ =\epsilon_s^2\int(B_{1,s}-B_{2,s})^2\dd\Omega
+  +o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+
+Finally, \(a_t,b_t\) are uniformly bounded below and
+\(|U_1|+|U_2|\le C\epsilon_s\).  Formula
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-H-third} consequently gives
+\[
+ \left|\frac{\dd^3}{\dd t^3}f(a_t,b_t)\right|
+ \le C\epsilon_s^3(1+a_t).
+\]
+Because \(\int a_t\dd\Omega=1\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound}
+ \sup_{0\le t\le1}|H'''(t)|\le C\epsilon_s^3
+ =o(\epsilon_s^2).
+\end{equation}
+Taylor's theorem, \eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-first-variation},
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-hessian-limit}, and
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-cubic-bound} expand \(H(1)\).  Combining
+that expansion with
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-remove-remainders} proves
+\eqref{eq:abstract-two-background-conclusion}.  Finiteness follows from the
+assumed positive lower bounds, the finite positive entropy of \(A_1\), and
+the fact that \(U_i,R_i\) are bounded perturbations; the negative part of
+\(a\log(a/b)\) is bounded in absolute integral by
+\(e^{-1}\int b\dd\Omega=e^{-1}\).
+\end{proof}

+The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
+entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
+finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
+quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
+tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact
+coefficient-attainment criterion.  The proof rests on critical weighted

+two-background Hessian argument.  This analytic architecture and its
+nonlocal-semigroup applications make the Journal of Functional Analysis a
+defensible first target.
